title: The energy in sunlight took at least tens of thousands of years to get out of the Sun
description:
Sunlight reaches you about eight minutes after leaving the Sun's surface. But the energy it carries spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out. Estimates include about 40,000 years (NASA SVS), 170,000 (Mitalas & Sills 1992) and about a million (NASA Marshall). The slow part is the crawl through the Sun's radiative zone; convection then carries it quickly to the surface. Deep inside, it travels mostly as X-rays. It leaves as sunlight.

Sources:
- Mitalas & Sills 1992, "On the Photon Diffusion Time Scale for the Sun", ApJ 401, 759. doi:10.1086/172103
- NASA Marshall, The Solar Interior: solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml
- NASA SVS, Origin of Light: svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084
- Stix 2003, Solar Physics 212, 3. doi:10.1023/A:1022952621810
- Christensen-Dalsgaard, Gough & Thompson 1991, ApJ 378, 413. doi:10.1086/170441
- IAU 2012 Resolution B2 (astronomical unit); CODATA 2022 (speed of light)
